© Digital Light Synthesis (DLS) is a form of additive manufacturing that utilizes light to
rapidly cure liquid resin into high-quality, 3D objects.

© Step 1: Ultraviolet (UV) light images are projected up into a pool of liquid resin,
where the object's first layer takes shape.

© Step 2: The partially cured resin object is raised, leaving a thin space (a “dead zone")
beneath it for oxygen and liquid resin to flow through.

© Step 3: The UV light passes through the dead zone—maintaining the flow of resin—
and partially cures additional layers of the object.

© Step 4: When the resin object is complete, it is baked in an oven to complete the
curing.
